subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Religion Peace Conflict Through A Study Of Islam Spec B
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Muslims believe that Jannah and Jahannam refer to:
options: Paradise and Hell in the afterlife
questions.explain: Jannah is Paradise and Jahannam is Hell, the two destinations after the Day of Judgement.

questions.q: In Islam, the first prophet and first man created by God was:
questions.explain: Muslims believe Adam was the first human and the first prophet created by God.

questions.q: Risalah in Islam refers to:
options: Prophethood and the messengers sent by God
questions.explain: Risalah is the belief in prophethood, that God sent prophets and messengers to guide humanity.

questions.q: The Arabic phrase 'subhanahu wa ta'ala', often said after Allah's name, expresses:
questions.explain: This phrase means 'glorified and exalted is he', showing reverence when Muslims mention God.

questions.q: Al-Qadr in Islam refers to:
options: God's predestination and the idea that he knows all that will happen
questions.explain: Al-Qadr is the belief in predestination, that God has knowledge of and decrees all events.

questions.q: Muslims believe earlier holy books such as the Tawrat and Injil were:
options: Revealed by God but the Qur'an is the final, complete revelation
Never sent by God at all
questions.explain: Muslims respect earlier scriptures as revelations from God, but hold the Qur'an as the final, complete message.

questions.q: Among Shia Muslims, the belief in Imamate is the belief in:
options: Divinely appointed leaders to guide the community after Muhammad
A new holy book after the Qur'an
questions.explain: Imamate is the Shia belief in divinely appointed Imams who lead and guide the Muslim community.

questions.q: Shia Muslims believe leadership should have passed to:
options: Ali, the cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad
questions.explain: Shia Muslims believe Ali, Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, was the rightful successor.

questions.q: Belief in Al-Qadr is sometimes debated because Muslims also believe that humans:
options: Still have free will and responsibility for their choices
Have no role in their actions
questions.explain: Despite belief in predestination, Muslims hold that humans have free will and are accountable for their actions.

questions.q: Muslims believe that on the Day of Judgement people will be given a record of their deeds in:
options: A book they receive in their right or left hand
questions.explain: The Qur'an describes people receiving a book of their deeds, in the right hand for the saved and the left for the condemned.

questions.q: The five roots of Usul ad-Din are the foundations of faith for:
questions.explain: The five roots of Usul ad-Din are the key beliefs that form the foundation of Shia Islam.

questions.q: For Muslims, the Qur'an is believed to be:
options: The direct word of God revealed to Muhammad
A book written after his death by historians
questions.explain: Muslims believe the Qur'an is the literal word of God revealed to the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.q: Which religious organisation is well known for helping victims of war and disaster?
questions.explain: Faith-based charities such as Christian Aid and Muslim Aid provide relief and support to victims of war and disaster.

questions.q: What does the just-war condition of 'proper authority' require?
options: War needs no authority at all
Only religious leaders may declare war
War must be declared by a legitimate government or authority, not by individuals
questions.explain: Just War theory requires that war be declared by a legitimate authority rather than by private individuals.

questions.q: Which is a religious response to the victims of war?
options: Providing charity, aid and shelter to those who suffer
questions.explain: Many believers feel a duty to help victims of war through aid, shelter and compassion.

questions.q: What is 'pacifism'?
options: The belief that violence and war are never justified
The belief that war is always right
questions.explain: Pacifism is the principled rejection of violence and war as a means of resolving conflict.

questions.q: Akhirah in Islam means:
questions.explain: Akhirah is the belief in life after death and an eternal existence beyond this life.

questions.q: On the Day of Judgement, Muslims believe people will be:
options: Judged by God on their deeds and sent to Paradise or Hell
questions.explain: Muslims believe God will judge each person by their actions, leading to Paradise or Hell.

questions.q: Malaikah in Islam are:
options: Angels who serve and obey God
questions.explain: Malaikah are angels, beings created by God who carry out his commands, such as Jibril.

questions.q: What does the 'proportionality' condition of Just War theory require?
options: Wars should last as long as possible
The force used should not exceed what is needed to achieve the aim
Maximum force should always be used
questions.explain: Proportionality requires that the force and harm used be no greater than necessary.

questions.q: Belief in Tawhid means Muslims reject:
options: Associating any partners or equals with God (shirk)
questions.explain: Because God is one, Muslims reject shirk, the sin of associating partners with God.

questions.q: Belief in Tawhid is reflected in Surah al-Ikhlas, which stresses that God is:
options: A father with a divine son
One, with no partner and nothing comparable to him
questions.explain: Surah al-Ikhlas declares the absolute oneness of God, stating there is nothing comparable to him.
